items.question_text: What is the definition of thermal conductivity?

options.a: The rate of energy transfer by conduction per unit area per unit temperature gradient
options.b: The amount of energy needed to raise 1 kg by 1 °C
options.c: The energy transferred by radiation each second
options.d: The temperature at which a material conducts

items.explanation: Thermal conductivity describes how quickly a material conducts energy.

items.question_text: An electric motor is supplied with \(2400\,\text{J}\) of energy. It transfers \(1800\,\text{J}\) usefully to the kinetic energy store of a fan. Calculate the efficiency of the motor as a percentage.

wrong.misconception: slip: gave the decimal when a percentage was asked

items.explanation: efficiency = useful output ÷ total input = 1800 ÷ 2400 = 0.75 = 75%.

items.question_text: Why does oiling the moving parts of a machine make it more efficient?

options.a: The oil adds extra energy to the moving parts
options.b: It lowers friction, so less energy is wasted as heat
options.c: It increases the total energy put into the machine
options.d: It stops energy from being conserved in the machine

feedback.a: Oil doesn't supply energy to the machine. It reduces friction, so less of the input energy is dissipated as heat.
feedback.c: The input energy is unchanged. Efficiency rises because less of it is wasted by friction.
feedback.d: Energy is always conserved. Lubrication just means less of it is dissipated to the surroundings as heat.

items.explanation: Lubrication reduces friction between moving parts, so less energy is dissipated as thermal energy and a greater fraction of the input energy is usefully transferred.

items.question_text: Motor X lifts a crate through a height of 2 m in 4 s. Motor Y lifts an identical crate through the same height in 8 s. Which statement is correct?

options.a: Motor X transfers more energy to the crate than motor Y.
options.b: Both motors transfer the same energy, but motor X has the greater power.
options.c: Motor Y has the greater power because it works for longer.
options.d: Motor Y transfers more energy because it takes longer.

feedback.a: The crates gain the same gravitational potential energy (same mass, same height). Power, not energy, is different.
feedback.c: Power is energy transferred per second. Taking longer means lower power.
feedback.d: The energy transferred depends on the change in the store, not on how long it takes.

items.explanation: Each crate gains the same Ep = mgh, so the energy transferred is equal. X transfers it in half the time, so X has twice the power (P = E/t).

items.question_text: A motor transfers 1200 J of energy in 30 s. What is its power?

feedback.a: This multiplies energy by time. Power is energy transferred per second: \(P = E \div t = 1200 \div 30 = 40\,\text{W}\).
feedback.c: This divides time by energy. Use \(P = E \div t = 1200 \div 30 = 40\,\text{W}\).
feedback.d: This adds the energy and the time. Power = energy ÷ time \(= 40\,\text{W}\).

items.explanation: Power = energy transferred ÷ time: \(P = 1200 \div 30 = 40\,\text{W}\).

items.question_text: A ball of mass \(0.50\,\text{kg}\) is dropped from a window \(3.2\,\text{m}\) above the ground. Air resistance can be ignored. Gravitational field strength \(g = 9.8\,\text{N/kg}\). Calculate the speed of the ball just before it hits the ground. Give your answer to 2 significant figures. [3 marks]

mark_scheme: Ek gained = Ep lost, so ½ × 0.50 × v² = 15.68 (1)

items.explanation: Energy is conserved: the Ep lost equals the Ek gained. mgh = ½mv², so v = √(2gh) = √(2 × 9.8 × 3.2) = 7.9 m/s.

items.question_text: A tro-tro of mass \(1200\,\text{kg}\) is travelling at \(15\,\text{m/s}\). How much kinetic energy does it have?

wrong.misconception: This forgets to square the speed. \(E_k = \tfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} = \tfrac{1}{2} \times 1200 \times 15^{2} = 135\,000\,\text{J}\).
This forgets the \(\tfrac{1}{2}\): \(E_k = \tfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}\), so halve \(1200 \times 225\) to get \(135\,000\,\text{J}\).
\(1200 \times 15 = 18\,000\) is the momentum (\(mv\)). Kinetic energy is \(\tfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} = 135\,000\,\text{J}\).

answer_spec.unit_feedback: Kinetic energy is energy, so it is measured in joules (J).
